### Design defaults

### Row and Col

Grid is maintained as one component-family document for the registered Row and Col. Row owns gutter, alignment, justification and wrapping; Col owns span, offset, order, flex and breakpoint configurations. Antd spans use a 24-column row. Plan normal and full-row allocations from actual available width, labels and content; account for offsets before deciding whether a row fits.

### Sizing and responsive use

The current Row control exposes numeric gutter; Col breakpoint controls expose objects. Read supported binding forms before using a native API shape beyond those controls. Do not assume CSS grid-template-columns or gap props apply to Row/Col. Use responsive Col configurations only when the task requires reflow, retaining authored reading order rather than using order to create a conflicting keyboard sequence.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

Check rendered gutter and cell edges, full-row/paired fields, longest values, error-expanded content and conditional cells. Apply Form layout for forms and shared layout for ownership. Test required widths near reflow boundaries, page overflow and save/reopen of real Row/Col props.

# Skeleton

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Skeleton | `plasmic-antd6-skeleton` |
| Skeleton.Avatar | `plasmic-antd6-skeleton-avatar` |
| Skeleton.Button | `plasmic-antd6-skeleton-button` |
| Skeleton.Image | `plasmic-antd6-skeleton-image` |
| Skeleton.Input | `plasmic-antd6-skeleton-input` |
| Skeleton.Node | `plasmic-antd6-skeleton-node` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for the first load of a region whose structure is known, matching that structure; remove it when data arrives.

### Initial loading structure

Use Skeleton when the actual initial content structure is known and placeholders help retain its layout. Match the expected region without inserting sample business values. Its registered loading default is true; bind real loading state so the delivered page does not remain a placeholder after data arrives. Use Spin when an indeterminate operation over existing content is more appropriate.

### Skeleton variants

Button, Input, Avatar, Image and Node registrations are sections of this family. They expose their own active contract; do not assume every native Skeleton prop is available on each variant. They are non-interactive placeholders and must not replace the real actionable controls after loading.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

Verify placeholder-to-content transition, realistic bounds, long content and failure recovery under content-state composition. Preserve the owning region's spacing and scroll reachability without a large layout jump or leftover duplicate children.

# Slider

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Slider | `plasmic-antd6-slider` |

## Generation rules

### Scalar and range values

The registered Slider uses a scalar for one handle and a numeric array for range mode. Read the actual range configuration, min/max/step, marks, tooltip and value/defaultValue contract. Keep numeric bounds and meaningful zero; do not silently round, clamp or add business restrictions beyond the requirement. A precise value may need an adjacent InputNumber, using one verified shared value owner.

### Events and acceptance

onChange reports interaction changes; onChangeComplete represents completion. Do not run an expensive business mutation on every movement when the requirement calls for a committed value. Test endpoints, step precision, keyboard changes, range ordering, disabled state and controlled/uncontrolled initialization. Verify marks and tooltip content at the required width and save/reopen bindings.

Components: plasmic-antd6-space, plasmic-antd6-space-compact
# Space

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Space | `plasmic-antd6-space` |
| Space.Compact | `plasmic-antd6-space-compact` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for an inline group of Buttons, Tags or short items: horizontal, size 8.
- Page and surface stacking uses Flex vertical with gap 16, not Space.

### Spaced siblings

Use Space for content-sized controls or inline groups; use Flex when children need to fill the remaining region. The v6 registration uses orientation, numeric size, wrap, align and separator. Set the intended gap once and inspect native child margins before adding it. A separator is part of the group, not an extra surface or heading.

### Space.Compact

Compact joins related controls through native borders and sizing; it does not create a business field or an ordinary gapped toolbar. Read orientation, size and block from its own registration. Keep each real Form field's ownership and accessible label. Do not place a Compact wrapper between a named Item and its bound control without the actual supported nested-Item pattern.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

Verify alignment, wrapping, joined borders, disabled controls, mixed content heights and long labels. Check width filling only where intended, no duplicated component margins and complete keyboard traversal. Follow shared layout for responsive and spacing decisions.

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Spin | `plasmic-antd6-spin` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use over a region whose content is being refreshed; first loading of a known structure uses Skeleton.

### Busy region

Use Spin for the actual busy region, keeping useful content visible during a background refresh when the flow permits it. spinning is business state; delay only controls presentation and must not become a submit lock. The native description, indicator, size and fullscreen controls follow this v6 registration.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

The child region needs meaningful bounds; Spin does not create its scroll or height contract. Verify first load, refresh, fast completion, failure and repeated use with content-state composition. Use fullscreen only for an actual page-wide blocked operation, preserve keyboard/focus behavior and remove the spinner when work settles.

### Resizable sibling panels

Use Splitter for a real user-resizable layout, with direct Splitter.Panel children in the registered Slot. The current registration uses orientation and onResize(sizes); panels expose defaultSize, min, max, resizable and collapsible. Read supported units and native size constraints rather than guessing them from an ordinary Flex layout.

### Ownership and acceptance

Splitter needs a meaningful bounded region from its container; the registration adds no default height. Each panel's content retains its own supported scroll contract without adding a parallel outer scrollbar. Verify drag and keyboard resize when supported, minimum/maximum size, collapse/restore, long content and action reachability. Persist panel size only when the workflow requires it; canvas selection must not alter saved business state.

Components: plasmic-antd6-statistic, plasmic-antd6-statistic-timer
# Statistic

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Statistic | `plasmic-antd6-statistic` |
| Statistic.Timer | `plasmic-antd6-statistic-timer` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for an emphasized number: a total, count or rate that the user reads first.
- The label goes in the title Slot (14px secondary), the unit in the suffix; value styling per metrics.
- Placement: four metric Cards per row in an overview, or beside or directly above the data it counts.

### Usage and behavior

Use the registered Statistic for emphasized numeric business values. Read its actual Props/Slots and apply typography through supported content styling; never invent a prop to force font size or replace required numeric content with decorative text.

Metric composition owns project typography defaults, label/value/unit roles, comparison placement and longest-content acceptance. Preserve complete values and legitimate zero.

### Statistic.Timer and acceptance

Timer uses its own type=countdown/countup, value, format and onFinish contract. The registered value is a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, not a duration or seconds. Displayed time does not prove an external operation completed; onFinish triggers only the consuming workflow's verified action. Do not recreate Timer as a constantly changing text expression or assume Statistic has Timer's value semantics.

Verify metric value/precision/prefix/suffix/loading with zero, long and missing values; verify Timer initialization, boundary/finish, reopening and the required callback policy. Keep title/unit/action ownership and complete readable values under the metric composition, then save/reopen actual bindings.

# Steps

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Steps | `plasmic-antd6-steps` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for a workflow with three to five ordered stages that the user moves through.
- Horizontal, at the top of the step-form Page, outside any Card; titles are short stage nouns; the current stage comes from the workflow state.

### Usage and behavior

Preserve the installed Ant Design default current step unless the requirement supplies an explicit value. Registration hints must not seed a different runtime current step.

### Stages and outcomes

Steps describes the actual workflow's stages through items/current/status, not a fabricated progression animation. Use stable stage meaning and distinguish current stage from completed/failed status. A click/onChange reports the requested stage; it does not validate the Form, save data or authorize skipping prerequisites by itself.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

Use step-form composition when stages own fields. Verify initial/current index, allowed forward/back transitions, errors, disabled stages as supported, long titles and the required orientation/size. Check changing content and saved business state rather than accepting only the visible step highlight.

# Switch

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |
| --- | --- |
| Switch | `plasmic-antd6-switch` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for a boolean field or a setting that takes effect immediately. A record state change in a Table uses row actions, unless the source draws an inline Switch.
- Content-sized; the label states the enabled meaning.

### Boolean field or immediate action

A Switch expresses a boolean on/off state. Read the registered checked/defaultChecked and onChange(checked) contract; do not bind value instead of checked. Inside a business Form, keep it as the real Item control and let Form own the field. An immediate server mutation is a separate workflow: permission, pending state, rejection recovery and confirmation come from the requirement rather than from the Switch itself.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

Exercise initial false/true, toggling, controlled and uncontrolled values, disabled behavior and the real Form payload. For an immediate action, verify exactly one mutation, the required pending policy and restored state after failure. The label must explain the enabled condition; apply keyboard/name checks.

Read the installed Tabs contract. Use actual items, never drawn tab labels. SearchForm + Tabs + Table owns independent/shared Table placement; Card spacing owns outer edge padding.

# Tag

| Registered component | Registration key |

| Tag | `plasmic-antd6-tag` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for categories only when the source shows them as chips, or for several labels on one record; a single ordinary value stays text; states use Badge.
- One fixed colour per category value, recorded with the reviewed mapping; never colour as the only meaning.

### Tag or text

Category is a business meaning, not a requirement to use Tag. Ordinary single-value attributes default to text, including type, market, source and department. A short enum or a field named “type” is insufficient reason to add a Tag. Lifecycle/processing states follow Badge.

| Source purpose and presentation | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary single-value classification with no requested emphasis | Text |
| Independent business labels, often several per record and read individually | Tag |

| Selected filter criteria that can be removed individually | Closable Tag; closing removes that criterion |
| A boolean selection expressed as a checkable label | Tag.CheckableTag |
| Name, identifier, time, amount or description | Text or its appropriate dedicated presentation |

Honor the current user's explicit presentation choice and applicable mandatory field rules; otherwise preserve the designated visual draft. This general Tag applicability guidance does not override a draft's plain text. Without a specified presentation, use the defaults above. | Tooltip | `plasmic-antd6-tooltip` |

### Design defaults

- Use for supplemental help on an icon, the complete value of truncated table text, or the meaning of a metric; never for required instructions or the only path to an action. Text columns expected to exceed their width follow the Column ellipsis + Tooltip pattern.

| Registered component | Registration key |

| Tree Select | `plasmic-antd6-tree-select` |

## Generation rules

### Design defaults

- Use for choosing from a hierarchy where any level can be selected; a fixed-depth path uses Cascader.
- Fills its column; `showSearch` above twenty nodes; `allowClear` in query and optional fields.

### Usage and behavior

Single/multiple/checkable values may be scalars, arrays or labeled objects. Registered state and event types must represent those modes. For wrapper changes, test actual mode/value combinations and controlled/uncontrolled behavior against the installed Ant Design version.

### Hierarchy and field ownership

Keep stable unique treeData values, readable titles and the actual parent/child structure. Selection values are not Cascader path arrays; do not flatten the hierarchy into copied labels. Read treeCheckable/multiple and any labeled-value contract before forming a payload. Inside Form, retain the owning Item's value/change binding.

## Acceptance checks

### Acceptance

Verify nested selection, parent/child check behavior, clearing, disabled controls, long labels, empty/reloaded options and selected-value recovery. Remote search/loading may use only a capability present in the current registration. Check actual scalar/array/object output, keyboard navigation and saved bindings in each required mode.

# Upload

| Registered component | Registration key |

The registered Upload uses files/onFilesChange with metadata, base64 contents and reading status. Its beforeUpload prevents native server uploading. dragAndDropFiles selects a drag surface within this same local wrapper. Read accept, multiple, maxCount, listType and showUploadList; file-size validation and persistence exist only when implemented in the consuming workflow. Remove and error states must retain the intended remaining files, and an accept hint does not certify file content.

### Upload.Dragger

The separately registered Dragger forwards native action/name/multiple/accept/disabled and onChange(info). It does not expose the local wrapper's files/onFilesChange/base64 model. A drag surface therefore does not establish which upload workflow is active. Keep both registrations here, select the actual one and bind its real transport/status contract. # Watermark

Library: Ant Design v6.

| Registered component | Registration key |

## Generation rules

### Required watermark region
